records.official_name: In the Strait of Bab el Mandeb

records.open_questions: Confirm any VTS at Perim/Djibouti; confirm VRA extent from UKMTO/MSCIO primary page (403). records.states: Oman; Iran (Islamic Republic of) (proposing States per IMO)
records.tss_identity_note: Proposed by Iran and Oman and adopted by IMO in 1968 (IMO page, 2026); included in A.284(VIII) (1973); amended scheme adopted by MSC 40 (IMCO circular dated 7 June 1979); reference chart changed to BA 3172 (WGS 84) by COLREG.2/Circ.33 (25 Feb 1994); inshore traffic zone off Musandam redescribed by COLREG.2/Circ.40 (implemented 24 Nov 1994). 2026 hostilities: IMO page confirms the TSS as 'existing'; press reports of temporary Omani routes north and south of the lanes are leads only and were not verified from an Omani Notice to Mariners.
records.vts_relationship_basis: No primary source establishing a VTS covering the IMO Hormuz TSS. Lead: search snippet (puertos.es document, HTTP 403) says Bandar Abbas VTC requires contact on VHF 13 before entering local 'TSS (area A/B)' between Larak, Hormuz and Qeshm, which appear to be port-approach lanes rather than the IMO scheme. Omani radar monitoring from Musandam is a press lead only.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: No IMO-adopted mandatory ship reporting system for the Strait of Hormuz found. Flag-State guidance recommends voluntary security reporting only.
records.voluntary_reporting: UKMTO daily reporting, MSCIO VRA registration and IFC-IOR voluntary reporting for vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz (Liberia MSB 14/2026); IMO page also points to UKMTO, JMIC and MSCIO advisories and Oman NAVAREA IX notices.
records.applicability_notes: Conflict-affected (2026); security level 3 advised by at least one flag State for Liberian ships. Recorded neutrally.
records.complexity_reason: Two-State strait, conflict-affected, temporary routeing reports, layered security reporting, possible Iranian port VTS overlap.
records.open_questions: Obtain Oman NAVAREA IX notices on temporary routes and any Omani/Iranian VTS covering the TSS; puertos.es document on Bandar Abbas VTS blocked (403). Current edition of IMO Ships' Routeing and UKHO ANM Section 17 not retrieved (UKHO download returned HTTP 500), so later amendments or revocations after the cited circular cannot be excluded.

records.official_name: At One Fathom Bank (with precautionary area 'Off Port Klang')
records.states: Malaysia (Straits of Malacca; system proposed by Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore)
records.tss_identity_note: Amended scheme adopted by MSC 69 (May 1998); COLREG.2/Circ.44 annex 1, implemented 0000 UTC 1 Dec 1998, with precautionary area 'Off Port Klang'. Segment of the Malacca-Singapore routeing system.
records.vts_relationship_basis: Scheme spans c. 03°02'.7N to 02°41'N (Circ.44). On the STRAITREP chartlet the Sector 1 (Angsa)/Sector 2 (Jugra) boundary runs at about 02°52'N towards Port Klang, so the scheme lies in Sectors 1 and 2, both 'Klang VTS' (MSC.73(69) para 3.4); VHF 66 (Sector 1) and 88 (Sector 2).
records.reporting_relationship_basis: STRAITREP (MSC.73(69), in force 1 Dec 1998) applies throughout the operational area, which 'includes the routeing system in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore'; reports to the VTS authority for the sector. Sectors 1-2: Klang VTS.
records.applicability_notes: STRAITREP participants: ships of 300 GT and above; 50 m or more in length; towing/pushing combinations of 300 GT or 50 m; any tonnage carrying hazardous cargo; all VHF-fitted passenger vessels; smaller VHF-fitted vessels using the lanes in an emergency (MSC.73(69) Annex 1 para 1.1).
records.complexity_reason: One VTS but two STRAITREP sectors/channels; part of a multi-State routeing and reporting system.
records.open_questions: Sector boundaries are published only as chartlets (MSC.73(69) appendices 1-2); allocation is by visual interpretation of the MPA 2026 chartlet against Circ.44 coordinates, not by stated boundary coordinates. Later amendments to the Malacca schemes after 1998 not checked. Operating authority of Klang and Johor VTS (Marine Department Malaysia) not stated in fetched sources; Malaysian sources not retrieved.
records.research_effort: approx 5 web actions (shared across TSS-0107 to 0110)

records.applicability_notes: STRAITREP participants: ships of 300 GT and above; 50 m or more in length; towing/pushing combinations of 300 GT or 50 m; any tonnage carrying hazardous cargo; all VHF-fitted passenger vessels; smaller VHF-fitted vessels using the lanes in an emergency (MSC.73(69) Annex 1 para 1.1).
records.complexity_reason: Single VTS; sector boundary near south-eastern end changes working channel.

Operating authority of Klang and Johor VTS (Marine Department Malaysia) not stated in fetched sources; Malaysian sources not retrieved.

records.official_name: Malacca to Iyu Kecil (with precautionary area 'Off Sultan Shoal Lighthouse')
records.states: Malaysia; Indonesia (south side of the strait)
records.tss_identity_note: New scheme adopted by MSC 69; COLREG.2/Circ.44 annex 4, implemented 1 Dec 1998, with precautionary area 'Off Sultan Shoal Lighthouse'. Continues eastward into 'In the Singapore Strait' (amended 2004, COLREG.2/Circ.54 annex 5, implemented 1 Jan 2005).
records.vts_relationship_basis: Scheme runs c. 02°05'N 102°04'E to 01°09'-01°14'N 103°27'-103°30'E. On the chartlets it crosses Sectors 4 (Undan) and 5 (Segenting) of Klang VTS (VHF 61, 88) and Sector 6 (Piai) of Johor VTS (VHF 88). Its eastern end meets the Tg Piai - Pulau Karimun Kecil line (reporting line, and Sector 6/7 boundary on Appendix 2); by the Circ.44 coordinates the easternmost lane ends lie marginally east of that line, in Sector 7 (Singapore VTS, VHF 73), where the associated Off Sultan Shoal precautionary area also lies. North-western end adjoins the Sector 3/4 boundary.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: STRAITREP (MSC.73(69), in force 1 Dec 1998) applies throughout the operational area, which 'includes the routeing system in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore'; reports to the VTS authority for the sector. Sectors 4-5 Klang VTS, Sector 6 Johor VTS; ships crossing the Tg Piai - Karimun Kecil line report on entering Singapore VTS Sector 7.
records.applicability_notes: STRAITREP participants: ships of 300 GT and above; 50 m or more in length; towing/pushing combinations of 300 GT or 50 m; any tonnage carrying hazardous cargo; all VHF-fitted passenger vessels; smaller VHF-fitted vessels using the lanes in an emergency (MSC.73(69) Annex 1 para 1.1).
records.complexity_reason: Crosses three or four STRAITREP sectors and two or three VTS authorities in two States, with a mandatory reporting line at its eastern end.
records.open_questions: Sector boundaries are published only as chartlets (MSC.73(69) appendices 1-2); allocation is by visual interpretation of the MPA 2026 chartlet against Circ.44 coordinates, not by stated boundary coordinates. Later amendments to the Malacca schemes after 1998 not checked. Operating authority of Klang and Johor VTS (Marine Department Malaysia) not stated in fetched sources; Malaysian sources not retrieved. Whether the Singapore VTS link should be treated as scheme coverage or only its terminus is a judgement for the editor.

batch_audits.classification_check: Four VTS and four reporting Confirmed present (Malacca), using existing names Klang VTS, Johor VTS, Singapore VTS, STRAITREP. Dondra: Unresolved/Provisional.
batch_audits.duplication_check: Klang VTS, Johor VTS, Singapore VTS map to register VTS-004/005/006; STRAITREP maps to SRS-004. Sectors not treated as separate services.
batch_audits.unresolved_items: Exact sector boundaries (chartlet-only); Singapore VTS link for TSS-0110 terminus; Dondra adoption instrument and any Sri Lankan VTS.

method_notes: Most efficient source: a Swedish Transport Agency PDF compiling scanned IMO COLREG.2 circulars (1978 to Circ.69), plus IMO Assembly resolutions A.284(VIII) and A.338(IX) on wwwcdn.imo.org; these gave adoption data for all Gulf/Oman/Red Sea/Malacca records. OCR is imperfect (quoted passages have spelling normalised where OCR garbled). UKHO ANM Section 17 download returned HTTP 500; Saudi Aramco port documents returned 404/403; UKMTO returned 403; the puertos.es document on Bandar Abbas VTS returned 403. STRAITREP sector boundaries exist only as chartlets (MPA Singapore Port Information 2026, Appendices 1-2), so segment-to-sector allocation is a visual interpretation cross-checked against Circ.44 coordinates; a Malaysian Marine Department or Royal Malaysian Navy (MAL 515/521/523) source would firm this up. Suggest the register treat voluntary security reporting (UKMTO/MSCIO/IFC-IOR) as a single regional voluntary overlay.
